about: Expected hash lines, byte for byte, for one fixture of every tag and every shape of line the fixtures give. A case is named after its scheme. The line of a case is in the file CASE.line beside this one and is what `archivewolf hash --mode MODE tests/fixtures/FIXTURE` writes. tests/golden_lines_test.rs compares them in the default test run. A line changes only with its format (section 7.6): record it again, compare it with the extractor again, crack it again, and say so under evidence.

evidence.extractors: Each line is the line the extractor of the hashcat fork writes for the same fixture: tools/zip2hashcat.py at feat/zip-modes 82a6718, tools/rar2hashcat.py at feat/rar-modes 0c9e37c, tools/7z2hashcat.py at feat/7z-modes 75a527f. Compared on 2026-11-18 by `make test-extractors` (tests/extractor_identity_test.rs), which compares them again on every run.
evidence.cracks: `make test-hashcat` (tests/hashcat_crack_test.rs) cracks every line whose case says crack: yes. Run on 2026-11-19 against a hashcat built from the three branches of the fork merged: 39 lines cracked and none failed. The crack_record of a case quotes an earlier record that names its fixture.

lines.why: A deflate stream that is in the line whole, 86 bytes, behind one header whose check byte is the top byte of the CRC-32: the line a cracker settles by inflating. Picked from the small deflate fixtures because the password of this one is recorded as found with mode 46100.
lines.crack_record: tests/fixtures/FIXTURES.md (ZIP passwords corrected on 2026-11-14): the password of this archive was found with hashcat mode 46100 and confirmed by unpacking. The line of that run was not kept, so it is not a crack of these bytes.

lines.why: A stored entry of 6 bytes, tested by its CRC-32, with the headers of the two other entries of the archive beside it: three checks, each with the file-time byte and the CRC byte as its alternative, as an archive with data descriptors needs. 136 characters.
lines.crack_record: tests/fixtures/FIXTURES.md (ZIP passwords corrected on 2026-11-14): the password of this archive was found with hashcat mode 46100 and confirmed by unpacking. The line of that run was not kept, so it is not a crack of these bytes.

lines.why: The only fixture marked as made by version 1.x, so the only one whose checks are two bytes wide: four hex digits behind each header. Two stored entries, of 300 and of 2 bytes.
Ten stored entries: the line carries the limit of eight checks and the 20 bytes of the first entry. The only fixture that reaches the limit.
bzip2: the line carries the first 32 bytes of a stream of 9,147, and the signature in them is what is tested. It stands for xz as well, whose line has the same shape. 130 characters.
LZMA, which hashcat does not unpack: the data field is empty and the check byte is all the line tests. The weak form of the line, 66 characters.
lines.crack: no: the line tests one byte, so a wrong word of the list passes once in 256 and a crack would prove nothing

lines.why: AES-128: strength 1 and a salt of 8 bytes. AE-2, 5 bytes of deflate with their authentication code. The smallest AES-128 line that carries data.
AES-192: strength 2 and a salt of 12 bytes. The smallest AES-192 line of the fixtures.
AES-256: strength 3 and a salt of 16 bytes. A stored entry of two bytes written by 7-Zip.
AE-1: extra field 0x9901 of the entry says version 1, and the entry keeps its CRC-32. The line has no field for that and is the line of AE-2; this one holds it so. 5 bytes of deflate under AES-256.
An empty entry: a packed size of 0 and no data, and still an authentication code to test.
PKWARE strong encryption with AES-128, the line of mode 46300, with the vector the decryption header stores: 32 hex digits. A stored entry.
AES-128 without a stored vector: the CRC-32 and the unpacked size stand in for it, 24 hex digits. A deflate entry.
AES-192, the line of mode 46310, with a stored vector. A deflate entry.
AES-192 without a stored vector. A stored entry.
AES-256, the line of mode 46320, with a stored vector. A deflate entry.
AES-256 without a stored vector. A stored entry.

The one strong encryption fixture that PKWARE's SecureZIP wrote; every other one comes from the generator of the hashcat test modules. AES-256, a stored vector, and validation data of 262 hex digits where the generator writes 32.
lines.crack: no: its password is not known

lines.why: RAR 1.5, a stored entry (method 30) of 87 bytes: the case hashcat checks on the device. From the junrar test files, 207 characters.
RAR 1.5, the same 87 bytes packed (method 33) to 84: the entry has to be unpacked before its CRC-32 can be compared.
RAR 2.0, a stored entry (method 30): 87 bytes in 96 bytes of block cipher data. From the junrar test files, 225 characters.
RAR 2.0, a packed entry (method 33): unpacked before its CRC-32 can be compared.

RAR 3 to 4 with encrypted headers (rar -hp): type 0, the salt and the 16 encrypted bytes of the end block, whose plaintext is known. Every such line of the fixtures is 83 characters; this is the archive named for RAR 4.20 and stored entries.

RAR 3 to 4 entry data (rar -p): type 1, 32 bytes packed with method 33, to be decrypted, unpacked and compared with the CRC-32. The smallest entry line of the fixtures, 116 characters. It is the line of b.txt, whose password is the one passwords.json has. No stored entry (method 30) is recorded: the three fixtures that give one give 868,794 characters each.
lines.crack_record: None names this line. tests/fixtures/FIXTURES.md records that the password of the other encrypted entry of this archive, d.txt, was found with hashcat mode 46700.

lines.why: RAR 5 entry (rar -p) whose header carries the password check value: type 0, nothing but salt, round count and the 8 bytes of the check value. The file is named for RAR 5.00. 109 characters.
RAR 5 with encrypted headers (rar -hp): type 0 from the encryption header of the archive. The same shape as the line of an entry, read from another place.
RAR 5 entry without a check value: type 1, check type 0, a stored entry of 300 bytes to decrypt and compare with its CRC-32.
Type 1, check type 1: the CRC-32 the archive stores is keyed with the password. The same stored entry of 300 bytes.
Type 1, check type 2: a BLAKE2sp digest of 64 hex digits in the place of the CRC-32.
Type 1, check type 3: the BLAKE2sp digest keyed with the password.

Type 1 with a packed entry (method 3): 5,632 bytes that have to be unpacked before the CRC-32 can be compared. The smallest packed entry without a check value among the fixtures whose password is recorded, and the longest line recorded here: 11,374 characters.
RAR 5 encrypted headers without a check value: type 1, check type 4, with 256 bytes of encrypted header blocks, tested by what they decrypt to.
A stored folder: no coder behind the cipher, 28 bytes, tested by the CRC-32. 133 characters.
LZMA2, what 7-Zip writes when it is not told otherwise: one coder in the chain. The same 28 bytes as the stored line.
LZMA with its five property bytes, and a vector of 8 bytes where 7-Zip now stores 16. The smallest such line whose password is known.
LZMA2 and then the x86 branch converter, in a folder of two files: two coders in the chain, and a CRC-32 that covers the first 28 of 74 bytes.
BCJ2: four packed streams, each with a vector and a chain of its own, joined by the BCJ2 coder. The smallest BCJ2 line, 407 characters.
Encrypted header (7zz -mhe=on): the line is made from the header, which is stored, with the CRC-32 the archive keeps for it. 293 characters.
Encrypted header that 7-Zip packed with LZMA before it encrypted it: a header line with a coder in its chain.
Encrypted header written by py7zr, which stores no CRC-32 for it: the CRC field holds the word header, and a candidate is tested by reading what it decrypts as a 7z header.
A salt of 4 bytes and 2^15 rounds, where 7-Zip writes no salt and 2^19. The only fixture with a salt; it is synthetic.
